info.title: OpenCRM
info.description: A CRM with companies, partners, contacts, customer users, and deal pipeline management.

customer_since.description: The day they became a customer (YYYY-MM-DD); null = not a customer. Set from the close date of their first won deal

renewal_date.description: The next renewal (YYYY-MM-DD); null = none. Within 30 days, or past, it shows on the Customers page

Partner.description: A firm that works deals with us (a reseller, a referrer, an integrator), kept apart from companies. Custom fields come as columns of their own, and relations under `relations`

status.description: Where the partnership stands: prospect (talking), onboarding (signing up, learning the product), active (working deals), inactive

deal_count.description: How many deals the partner takes part in

CustomerUser.description: A person who uses the product at a customer (a company with customer_since), kept apart from contacts. Custom fields come as columns of their own, and relations under `relations`

company_id.description: The customer they use the product at

last_contacted_at.description: Newest synced email with this contact (Gmail sync). Read-only

color.description: Palette token: sky, emerald, amber, rose, violet, fuchsia, teal, orange, slate

is_won.description: 1 = a deal here counts as won (fires the Slack alert)

is_lost.description: 1 = a deal here counts as lost (excluded from pipeline value)

at.description: The meeting's start (ISO 8601) or the task's due day (YYYY-MM-DD)

owed_by.description: Who owes a task; null for a meeting

NextStep.description: The soonest of the next meeting booked with the deal's company and its open tasks with a date. Null: nobody agreed on what happens next.

reasons.description: Why, worst first, in plain words. Empty when on track.

last_touch_at.description: The latest call, email or logged touch with the deal's company

DealProgress.description: How an open deal is moving (board and single-deal reads). Null for a won or lost deal.

value.description: What the deal is worth once

recurring_value.description: What the deal is worth each month while they stay a customer

owner_id.description: The account the deal is assigned to (GET /api/team); null = nobody yet

owner.description: The account the deal is assigned to

partners.description: The partners taking part in the deal, by name, each with its share of the deal

domain.description: Always null: partners have no domain

meeting_id.description: The call it was promised in

owed_by.description: us = we promised it; them = we're waiting on them

quote.description: The words in the call it came from

created_by.description: ai while the task follows its call's company; otherwise the person who created it or moved it

status.description: unknown: nothing against the account, but the CRM can't see whether anyone has been in touch (the reasons say why)

reasons.description: Why the status, worst first. Empty when on track

state.description: From the stage's flags; a stage not in the pipeline counts as open

bearerAuth.description: A personal API token, crm_…; it acts as its owner.

dealRecurringValue.description: What the deals not lost are worth each month

customerUsers.description: The people who use the product at customers

get.summary: Open deals, worst first: each one's next step and the reasons to look at it
get.description: An open deal is one whose stage is neither won nor lost. Its next step is the soonest of the next meeting booked with its company and its open tasks with a date (ours or theirs). Red: one of our promises is overdue, the last call went badly, a risk is open, or no next step and no contact in 14 days. Yellow: no next step, no contact in 14 days, waiting on them, the close date has passed, or the mood dropped. Contact is a call, an email, or a call, message, email or meeting logged on the deal, its company or its contacts; silence is judged only through what the CRM can see, and the reason says what it can't. Unknown: nothing against the deal and no way to judge contact.

schema.description: Viewer's UTC offset in minutes (e.g. 120), for what counts as overdue today

200.description: Open deals, worst first, then the biggest

calls.description: seen: on and working; off; importing: the first import hasn't finished; failing: the latest run failed

emails.description: seen: on and working; off; importing: the first import hasn't finished; failing: the latest run failed

post.summary: Log what happened on a deal, what it finished, and its next step
post.description: One call for an update the CRM can't read on its own (a phone call, a message, an email from another inbox, a meeting moved or held in person, or a note). It goes on the deal's timeline at the time it happened. done_task_ids marks open tasks the update finished. next_step adds what happens next as a task on the deal, with its date and who owes it. close_date moves the expected close. A call, message, email or meeting counts as contact with the deal's company; a note does not. Move the stage with PUT /api/deals/{id}.

kind.description: call, message, email, meeting: contact with them. note: anything else worth keeping.

summary.description: What happened, in a sentence or two: who, and what was said or agreed

at.description: When it happened: ISO 8601, or YYYY-MM-DD. Default now. Never in the future: what will happen goes in next_step.

done_task_ids.description: Open tasks of this deal (GET /api/tasks?deal_id=) that the update finished

next_step.description: What happens next, by when, and who owes it: added as a task on the deal

close_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, when the expected close moved

201.description: Logged; the deal with its progress, and the next-step task

get.summary: How each customer is doing (worst first) and why, what to do first, and what the CRM can see of calls and email
get.description: A customer is a company with customer_since set. Red: one of our promises is overdue, the last call went badly, a risk is open, or no contact in 45 days. Yellow: no contact in 21 days, waiting on them, the mood dropped, a renewal within 30 days (or past), or no contact yet. Silence is judged only through what the CRM can see (calls when the meeting sync is on, emails when the email sync is on and has read the account's contacts), and the reason names what it can't see. Unknown: nothing else against the account and no channel to judge it by.

schema.description: Viewer's UTC offset in minutes (e.g. 120), for what counts as overdue today

sight.description: Whether the CRM can see calls and emails at all

get.summary: What the CRM knows about an email address before someone writes to it
get.description: The contact with exactly this address; their company (else the company on `domain`, else on the address's own domain when it is a work address), with customer_since when it is a customer; the company's and the contact's deals (open first, at most 10); the latest call with the company (a synced meeting, or a call or meeting logged by hand; emails are left out, since an app that sends logs its own sends here); and the next meeting booked. Nulls and an empty list when the CRM has never heard of them. Read only.

schema.description: The company's domain, when the address is a personal one or the company is known by another domain

post.summary: What the CRM knows about up to 100 addresses at once
post.description: The answer GET /api/lookup gives, for each address in the order asked. For an app checking a batch of people before they join a campaign. An address with neither email nor domain gets an empty answer.

200.description: One answer per address, in order
